title: The UGLY Truth About Dropshipping That No Guru Will Tell You
summary: FAQ on dropshipping economics: legal but needs registration, ten-to-thirty percent margins, supplier dependence, marketplace bans for retail arbitrage, best used to test products before private labeling.

assertions.quote: the margins for drop shipping are much less than other e-commerce business models
you are actually responsible for processing returns and providing customer service for defective merchandise
aliexpress drop shipping on amazon is expressly prohibited

verdicts.note: Amazon and eBay policies prohibit drop-shipping from other retailers and suspend violators.

Amazon permits dropshipping only if the store owner, not the third-party retailer, is seller of record; Empire's retail-arbitrage dropshipping routinely violated this and Amazon suspended most of its stores within months for dropshipping-policy and IP violations.

assertions.quote: your drop shipping business is a real business and must be registered as such

verdicts.note: Sales-tax nexus and licensing rules apply to any online merchant.

assertions.quote: it's approximately the same amount of work to make a hundred bucks a month as it is to make a hundred thousand dollars a month

verdicts.note: Fulfillment scales, but customer service, ad spend and supplier management grow with volume.
Ad spend, customer service, refunds and supplier problems all grow with volume, so the work is not the same at any scale.

assertions.quote: you should use drop shipping as a stepping stone to create your own branded products for sale

verdicts.note: Strategic advice rather than a testable claim.

assertions.quote: you will face pricing pressure from other competing retailers offering the exact same goods
customer service product quality and delivery is entirely at the mercy of your drop ship supplier
